title: Tria capita ex opere quodam majori inedito de theoria lunae

deep.reconstruction:
Problem: correct the lunar tables from lunar eclipse observations without reducing the Moon's place to the ecliptic.

Setup (from §§3-6): on the sphere, with the node ☊ treated as fixed, ☊Ss is the ecliptic and ☊Ll the lunar orbit, inclined at the angle ρ. At the first contact the shadow centre is at S and the Moon's centre at L; at the last contact they are at s and l, h hours later. Both separations equal α+β (or α−β for immersion/emersion in a total eclipse), so SL = sl. The radius itself need not be known. Motions are taken uniform and relative to the node: the shadow moves (m+k)" per hour and the Moon (n+k)" per hour, k being the regression of the node.

§7: Euler chooses the instant t (hours after first contact) at which the Moon's argument of latitude equals the shadow's longitude from the node: ☊σ = ☊λ = x. This is not the true opposition, which would need reduction to the ecliptic. At that instant the lunar orbital longitude must equal the known longitude of the antisolar point, which is exactly what tables in orbital longitude must reproduce. Then:
- ☊S = x−(m+k)t
- ☊L = x−(n+k)t
- ☊s = x+(m+k)(h−t)
- ☊l = x+(n+k)(h−t)

The spherical law of cosines in triangles S☊L and s☊l (common angle ρ at the node) gives
cos SL = cosρ sin☊L sin☊S + cos☊L cos☊S,
and likewise for sl. Equating SL = sl yields
cos☊L cos☊S − cos☊l cos☊s = cosρ (sin☊l sin☊s − sin☊L sin☊S).

§8: angle-subtraction and angle-addition expansions, then product-to-sum formulas.

§9: The differences and sums are
- ☊S−☊L = (n−m)t and ☊l−☊s = (n−m)(h−t), both independent of x;
- ☊S+☊L = 2x−Mt and ☊s+☊l = 2x+M(h−t), with M = m+n+2k.

Substituting and collecting gives
(1+cosρ)[cos(n−m)t − cos(n−m)(h−t)] = (1−cosρ)[cos(2x+M(h−t)) − cos(2x−Mt)].

The next page expands for small angles (g = sin 1") and solves perturbatively:
t = h/2 + M sin2x tan²(ρ/2) / (g(n−m)²) + O(tan⁴(ρ/2)).
So the instant of equal orbital and shadow longitudes follows the eclipse middle by a term proportional to tan²(ρ/2) sin2x. This is the familiar 'reduction to the ecliptic' term, scaled by the relative motions.
errors: None on this page. Each angle-sum/difference expansion, product-to-sum identity, the sums/differences in §9 and the final rearrangement check out: with A = cos(n−m)t − cos(n−m)(h−t) and B = cos(2x−Mt) − cos(2x+M(h−t)), one gets A+B = cosρ(B−A), hence (1+cosρ)A = −(1−cosρ)B, as printed.
Notation: (m+k)t'' denotes the arc (m+k)·t in arcseconds, not t to the second power.

ideas.what: Using only the equality of the contact distances (SL = sl), not their value, to locate a lunar position, so the shadow radius and lunar semidiameter drop out.
ideas.modern_name: Differential/symmetric reduction of eclipse contact timings (eliminating unknown radii)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard 18th-c. eclipse reduction practice (Halley, Mayer, Euler and others), in various forms
ideas.where_published: Opera postuma (1862), E838; similar eclipse-based table corrections appear in Euler's lunar work but exact parallel unsure

ideas.what: Choosing the instant when the argument of latitude equals the shadow's longitude from the node, instead of the true opposition, to avoid reduction to the ecliptic.
ideas.modern_name: Comparison in orbital longitude (argument of latitude) rather than ecliptic longitude
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in lunar table practice; the explicit device here is Euler's
ideas.where_published: E838 (Opera postuma I, 1862; Opera omnia ser. II, lunar theory volume)

ideas.what: Spherical law of cosines in node-vertex triangles plus product-to-sum identities, isolating x-independent differences and 2x-dependent sums.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Euler systematised spherical trigonometry, E214 etc.)

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but routine spherical-trigonometric derivation within Euler's unfinished lunar theory. The device of using equal orbital/ecliptic longitudes is neat. It leads (next page) to the standard tan²(i/2) sin2u reduction term, which is well known. Nothing appears new to specialists.
